Scope: collector and local roads; potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, TSE, medium-voltage, street lighting and telecom networks; a sewage pump station and storm drainage ponds; boundary fence, guard room and utility buildings.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 09-Nov-2026 data date the construction works (131,328 budgeted man-hours, the basis used in earlier weeks) are 25.7% complete against 38.8% planned (SPI 0.66). This week added 4.62%, from storm drainage, the fence, utility buildings and sewage. The report's dashboard now also counts engineering, procurement and testing man-hours and gives 26.9% against 52.1% planned (SPI 0.52) on that wider basis.

The schedule update now finishes the project almost five months late. The P6 update with data date 09-Nov-2026 schedules project completion on 27-Jul-2027, 144 days after the contract completion date of 05-Mar-2027 and 5 days later than last week's update, with −116 days of total float. The weekly report's milestone table now shows the same finish, but its key dates still forecast 05-Mar-2027. Finishing on time needs about 4.6% physical progress a week for the 16 weeks left; this week's 4.62% is the first week at that rate.

This week the dashboard gives the same planned and recovery-planned man-hours (51,014), so the planned column serves as both. The 6,063 man-hours earned this week came from storm drainage (+2,090), the fence (+1,966), utility buildings (+1,004) and sewage (+1,002); roads did not move. The P6 update (data date 09-Nov-2026) has 1,065 activities: 380 completed, 50 in progress and 635 not started, against 302, 28 and 735 last week.

Data notes

  • This-week values compare the 09-Nov-2026 weekly report (WPR-38) with the 02-Nov-2026 report (WPR-37) in the W06 folder.
  • The Milestones sheet states contract week 44 of 60, used as the report week. Whole weeks from site handover to the data date give 43.
  • The dashboard changed its physical progress basis this week: it now adds engineering, procurement and testing man-hours (212,314 in total; the Progress sheet divides by 218,880 and the chart data by 218,514) and reports 26.9% actual against 52.1% planned. Compared with last week's 21.1% on the construction basis, that would show a jump that site work does not explain, so this report keeps the construction basis (131,328 man-hours): 25.7% against 38.8%.
  • The dashboard's planned and recovery-planned man-hours are now identical (51,014 for construction). Several WBS plans fell against last week (storm drainage 11,196 to 6,441, utility buildings 11,022 to 7,299) while others rose (potable water 560 to 3,715, irrigation 120 to 2,456).
  • Irrigation has 2,840 budgeted man-hours in the dashboard but 5,946 in the Progress sheet's P6 extract.
  • The weekly physical columns still repeat 708 planned and 445 earned man-hours (fence only). This week's gain (6,063 man-hours, +4.62%) was taken from the change in cumulative earned man-hours; it comes with no change in the Major Quantities sheet and no inspection log entries after 03-Nov-2026.
  • The Major Quantities and Procurement sheets are unchanged since 26-Oct-2026, and the supply tracking file is the same file as last week.
  • The supply tracking file gives much higher supplied quantities than the Procurement sheet, uses project ID DHRT-02-01 and names a different project manager ("م/ نواف"). It lists supplied quantities for storm manholes and catch basins that it also marks as still in manufacturing.
  • The weekly report's key dates forecast completion on 05-Mar-2027 with zero variance, while its milestone table and the P6 update give 27-Jul-2027 (22-Jul-2027 last week). The milestone table's network and approval forecasts are last week's P6 dates.
  • In the dashboard's progress overview, the Roads and CCTV rows have their names swapped; the Progress sheet was used instead.
  • The Conclusion sheet, the dashboard and the MODON project summary label cost-based progress as "actual" progress; it is not used in this report.
  • The Conclusion sheet is headed "Dammam", reports 260,000 m³ of earthworks against 428,344 m³ in the Major Quantities sheet, and gives network lengths that differ from the Procurement sheet (for example storm pipes 4,838 m against 4,672 m).
  • The MODON project summary gives other quantities again (earthworks 400,000 m³, storm network 1,500 m, sewage network 200 m), a contract end of 06-Mar-2027 and a target end of 31-Dec-2026.
  • The contract value cells in the dashboard and the invoice log now show #REF!. The invoice summary says 3 invoices were submitted, but the invoice log lists 4 with a total of 10,524,342 SAR; the MODON project summary gives 17,618,822 SAR in 3 invoices. The log also shows a revised contract value of 21,100,000 and an EAC of 20,900,000, which do not match this contract.
  • Several sheets carry other projects' identifiers or old dates: the QC checklist and the FIR log use project DHRT-02-001, the risk register uses DAMT-01-002 (Dammam), and the HSE inspection covers 27-Jan to 03-Feb-2026.
  • The issue log closes the advance payment issue, but the P6 update and the risk log both show it as still open.
  • November manual head count jumped from 30 to 224, including 130 operators and drivers, and equipment from 16 to 142, including 100 trailers; the dashboard's trade panel lists 54 workers and 125 pieces of equipment. The dashboard's resources panel still shows January head counts.
  • The Schedule sheet still counts 1,271 activities with the same statistics as in earlier weeks; the uploaded P6 file has 1,065.
  • One of the four photos is the same file as a photo in last week's workbook.
  • The uploaded PowerPoint is the MODON report guide; it still states contract week 35 of 60 and was not used for figures.
